questions.question: The McMahon Line is associated with which international agreement or convention?
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line was proposed in the 1914 Simla Convention for the eastern sector. China disputes it, while India regards it as the boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which country disputes the McMahon Line, according to the source?
questions.explanation: The source states that China disputes the McMahon Line, while India regards it as the boundary in the eastern sector.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Durand Line forms the boundary between which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Durand Line is the Afghanistan–Pakistan boundary and is not an India border.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the boundary line with its significance?

options.A: Radcliffe Line — India-China contested boundary alignment
options.B: LoC — military control line in Jammu and Kashmir between India and Pakistan
options.D: Durand Line — partition boundary between India and Pakistan

questions.explanation: The LoC is the military control line in Jammu and Kashmir between India and Pakistan. The other options incorrectly describe the respective lines.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?

options.A: Radcliffe Line — Partition of British India
options.D: LAC — India–Pakistan military control line in Jammu and Kashmir

questions.explanation: The LAC refers to the contested boundary alignment between India and China. The India–Pakistan military control line in Jammu and Kashmir is the LoC.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes?
questions.explanation: Zoji La is included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following passes is included in the source's list of important Himalayan passes?
questions.explanation: Banihal is one of the important Himalayan and international border passes listed in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pass appears in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes?
questions.explanation: Rohtang is included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an important Himalayan pass in the source?
questions.explanation: Baralacha La is included among the important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shipki La is included in which category in the source?

options.B: Important Himalayan and international border passes

questions.explanation: Shipki La is named in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following passes is included in the source's list besides Nathu La?
questions.explanation: Jelep La is listed among the important Himalayan and international border passes in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pass is included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes?
questions.explanation: Lipulekh is one of the passes named in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following pairs contains two passes included in the source's list?
questions.explanation: Both Mana and Niti are included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair of passes is included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes?
questions.explanation: Bum La and Se La are both named in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of passes named in the source?

options.A: Zoji La, Banihal, Rohtang and Baralacha La
options.B: Bhor Ghat, Thal Ghat, Palghat and Zoji La
options.C: Palghat, Bhor Ghat, Rohtang and Thal Ghat
options.D: Thal Ghat, Palghat, Bhor Ghat and Banihal

questions.explanation: Zoji La, Banihal, Rohtang and Baralacha La are all included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only passes listed in the source?

options.A: Shipki La, Jelep La, Lipulekh and Mana
options.B: Bhor Ghat, Palghat, Thal Ghat and Shipki La
options.C: Palghat, Bhor Ghat, Mana and Thal Ghat
options.D: Thal Ghat, Jelep La, Bhor Ghat and Palghat

questions.explanation: Shipki La, Jelep La, Lipulekh and Mana are all included in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only passes included in the source's list?

options.A: Niti, Bum La, Se La and Nathu La
options.B: Bhor Ghat, Thal Ghat, Palghat and Niti
options.C: Palghat, Bhor Ghat, Se La and Thal Ghat
options.D: Thal Ghat, Palghat, Bum La and Bhor Ghat

questions.explanation: Niti, Bum La, Se La and Nathu La are all named in the source's list of important Himalayan and international border passes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the LAC and the LoC is correct according to the source?

options.A: Both are partition boundaries created in 1947
options.B: The LAC refers to the India-China contested boundary alignment, while the LoC is the India-Pakistan military control line in Jammu and Kashmir
options.C: The LAC is the Afghanistan-Pakistan boundary, while the LoC is the India-Nepal boundary
options.D: Both are mutually demarcated international boundaries between India and China

questions.explanation: The source distinguishes the LAC as the contested boundary alignment between India and China and the LoC as the military control line in Jammu and Kashmir between India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. India's Standard Meridian is 82°30′E. 2. It passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. 3. India uses multiple civil time zones because of its longitudinal extent. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. India uses one standard time throughout the country, even though local solar time differs by nearly two hours between the eastern and western extremities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements about India's continental shelf: 1. It is the submerged natural prolongation of land territory. 2. Coastal states have sovereign rights over its seabed and subsoil resources. 3. Its outer limits may, under specified criteria, be established beyond 200 nautical miles. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are supported by the source's description of the continental shelf under UNCLOS.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas were formed by the convergence and collision of which two tectonic plates?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the convergence and collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The formation of the Himalayas followed the closure of which ancient ocean?
questions.explanation: The source explains that the Himalayas formed after the closure of the Tethys Ocean, when sediments in the former ocean basin were compressed, folded, faulted and uplifted.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the Himalayan region considered tectonically active?

options.A: The region is composed entirely of coral deposits
options.B: The collision and uplift of the Indian and Eurasian plates continue
options.C: The region is free from geological movement
options.D: The Himalayas are ancient volcanic plateaus

questions.explanation: The collision and uplift of the Indian and Eurasian plates continue, making the Himalayan region tectonically active.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the correct north-to-south sequence of the major longitudinal Himalayan belts given in the source?

options.A: Shiwalik – Lesser Himalaya – Greater Himalaya – Trans-Himalaya
options.B: Trans-Himalaya – Greater Himalaya – Lesser Himalaya – Shiwalik
options.C: Greater Himalaya – Trans-Himalaya – Shiwalik – Lesser Himalaya
options.D: Lesser Himalaya – Shiwalik – Trans-Himalaya – Greater Himalaya

questions.explanation: From north to south, the broad belts are Trans-Himalaya, Greater Himalaya (Himadri), Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) and Shiwalik.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan belt includes the Karakoram, Ladakh and Zanskar ranges?
questions.explanation: The Trans-Himalaya lies north of the Great Himalaya and includes the Karakoram, Ladakh and Zanskar ranges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan range is also known as Himadri?
questions.explanation: The Greater Himalaya is also called Himadri. It is the highest and most continuous Himalayan range.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan belt is described as having an average height commonly above 6,000 metres?
questions.explanation: The Greater Himalaya or Himadri is the highest and most continuous range, with average height commonly above 6,000 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar are associated with which Himalayan belt?
questions.explanation: The Lesser Himalaya, also known as Himachal, includes complex lower ranges such as Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Himalayan range is described as the outermost and youngest foothill range?
questions.explanation: The Shiwalik is the outermost and youngest foothill range of the Himalayas. It consists of unconsolidated sediments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The longitudinal valleys called duns are particularly associated with which Himalayan range?
questions.explanation: The Shiwalik range is associated with longitudinal valleys called duns.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states and regions is associated with the Western Himalayas in the source?

options.B: Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
options.C: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram

questions.explanation: The Western Himalayas extend across Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following regions is included in the Eastern Himalayas according to the source?
questions.explanation: The Eastern Himalayas extend across Sikkim, northern West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Compared with the Western Himalayas, the Eastern Himalayas are generally described as:
questions.explanation: The source characterises the Eastern Himalayas as generally wetter and having high biodiversity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Purvanchal Hills represent which geographical feature?

options.A: The western extension of the Aravalli Range
options.B: The eastern extension of the Himalayan hill system
options.C: The southern extension of the Western Ghats
options.D: The northern edge of the Deccan Plateau

questions.explanation: The Purvanchal Hills are the eastern extension of the Himalayan hill system, curving southward along India's northeastern frontier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of hills included in the Purvanchal system?

options.A: Patkai, Naga, Manipur and Mizo Hills
options.B: Aravalli, Vindhya, Satpura and Nilgiri Hills
options.C: Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Zanskar and Ladakh
options.D: Garo, Khasi, Jaintia and Nilgiri Hills

questions.explanation: The Purvanchal system includes the Patkai, Naga, Manipur and Mizo (Lushai) hills.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which peak is identified in the source as India's highest peak wholly within India?
questions.explanation: The source identifies Kangchenjunga, in the Sikkim–Nepal border region, as India's highest peak wholly within India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which country is Mount Everest located, according to the source?
questions.explanation: The source states that Mount Everest lies in Nepal and is not in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is named as an important Himalayan peak in the source?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi is included in the source's list of important Himalayan peaks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is fed by the Gangotri Glacier according to the source?
questions.explanation: The source states that the Gangotri Glacier feeds the Bhagirathi River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river system is fed by the Yamunotri Glacier?
questions.explanation: The Yamunotri Glacier feeds the Yamuna system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the source's list of important Himalayan glaciers?
questions.explanation: Zemu is one of the important Himalayan glaciers listed in the source, along with Siachen, Gangotri, Yamunotri, Pindari, Milam and Bara Shigri.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Changes in snow and ice storage in Himalayan glaciers have a direct effect on which major concern?
questions.explanation: The source notes that glacier retreat and changes in snow and ice storage affect downstream water security.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an important climatic role of the Himalayas?

options.A: They influence monsoon circulation and rainfall
options.B: They eliminate all seasonal rainfall variations
options.C: They prevent the formation of perennial rivers
options.D: They produce uniform temperatures throughout India

questions.explanation: The Himalayas influence monsoon circulation and rainfall and also act as a climatic barrier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an important role of the Himalayas in the source?

options.B: Storing freshwater in snow and glaciers
options.D: Eliminating the need for irrigation in all regions

questions.explanation: The source identifies river systems, freshwater storage, forests, biodiversity, hydropower, tourism and strategic significance as important Himalayan roles. It does not state that the Himalayas eliminate the need for irrigation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the abbreviation GLOF stand for in the context of Himalayan environmental hazards?
questions.explanation: GLOF stands for glacial lake outburst flood, identified in the source as a major environmental concern in the Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only environmental problems listed for the Himalayan region?

options.A: Glacier retreat, GLOFs, landslides and earthquakes
options.B: Coral bleaching, coastal erosion, tsunamis and salinity
options.C: Desertification, dune migration, dust storms and sea-level rise
options.D: Cyclones, coastal flooding, marine pollution and coral mining

questions.explanation: The source lists glacier retreat, glacial lake outburst floods, landslides and earthquakes among the major Himalayan environmental concerns.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which human activity is identified in the source as contributing to environmental pressure in the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: Unplanned tourism is listed among the major environmental concerns affecting the Himalayan region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the source, which combination increases hazard exposure in the Himalayan region?

options.C: Stable geology and absence of rivers

questions.explanation: The source explains that fragile geology and intense rainfall increase hazard exposure in the Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are duns?

options.B: Longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik ranges
options.C: Coastal lagoons along the eastern coast
options.D: Glacial lakes in the Greater Himalaya

questions.explanation: Duns are longitudinal valleys located between the Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik ranges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a dun mentioned in the source?
questions.explanation: Dehradun, Kotli Dun and Patli Dun are examples of duns given in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic of duns is specifically mentioned in the source?

options.A: They often contain alluvial deposits and relatively level land
options.B: They are entirely covered by permanent snow
options.C: They are formed exclusively by coral accumulation

questions.explanation: The source notes that duns often contain alluvial deposits and relatively level land.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological feature provided accommodation space for the thick alluvial deposits of the Northern Plains?

options.B: A foredeep south of the Himalayas
options.D: A rift valley in the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Subsidence of the foredeep south of the Himalayas created accommodation space for sediments over geological time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of river systems contributed the thick alluvial deposits that formed the Northern Plains?
questions.explanation: The Northern Plains were built by thick alluvial deposits brought by the Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra and their tributaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is one of the three broad divisions of the Northern Plains?
questions.explanation: The three broad divisions are the Punjab–Haryana Plain, Ganga Plain and Brahmaputra Plain.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Punjab–Haryana Plain is associated with which river system?
questions.explanation: The source associates the Punjab–Haryana Plain with the Indus river system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of physical and geographical conditions supports agriculture in the Northern Plains?

options.A: Deep alluvial soils, level terrain and abundant surface and groundwater
options.B: Steep slopes, shallow rocky soils and very low water availability
options.C: Permanent snow cover and frozen soils
options.D: Sand dunes, saline soils and absence of rivers

questions.explanation: The Northern Plains are agriculturally productive because of fertile alluvium, flat relief and abundant surface and groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following crops is specifically listed in the source as being supported by agriculture in the Northern Plains?
questions.explanation: The source lists rice, wheat, sugarcane, pulses and oilseeds among the crops supported by the Northern Plains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a constraint on agriculture in the Northern Plains?

options.C: Lack of surface water throughout the region

questions.explanation: The source identifies floods, waterlogging, groundwater depletion and soil salinity as important agricultural constraints in the Northern Plains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is specifically identified as having flood-prone areas in the Northern Plains?
questions.explanation: The source identifies low-lying floodplains in Assam, Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh and parts of West Bengal as flood-prone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination of factors is identified in the source as influencing flooding in the Northern Plains?

options.A: Intense monsoon rainfall, Himalayan sediment loads, channel migration, embankments and drainage constraints
options.B: Coral growth, ocean salinity and volcanic eruptions
options.C: Desert winds, coastal tides and marine currents
options.D: Glacier-free mountains and the absence of tributaries

questions.explanation: The source explains that flooding is influenced by intense monsoon rainfall, Himalayan sediment loads, channel migration, embankments and drainage constraints.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological age and rock composition best describe the Peninsular Plateau?

options.A: A young sedimentary region composed mainly of recent alluvium
options.B: An ancient stable block mainly composed of Precambrian igneous and metamorphic rocks
options.C: A recent volcanic island chain composed entirely of coral
options.D: A young fold mountain system composed mainly of marine sediments

questions.explanation: The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient, stable block of the Indian landmass, mainly composed of Precambrian igneous and metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which description correctly represents the general shape and slope of the Peninsular Plateau?

options.A: Circular and higher in the east, sloping westward
options.B: Triangular, higher in the west and sloping eastward
options.D: Triangular, higher in the south and sloping northward

questions.explanation: The Peninsular Plateau is generally triangular, higher in the west and slopes eastward. It contains broad valleys, residual hills and mineral-rich formations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Central Highlands are located on which side of the Narmada River?
questions.explanation: The Central Highlands lie north of the Narmada River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following plateaus is included in the Central Highlands?
questions.explanation: The Central Highlands include the Malwa Plateau, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand and Chota Nagpur Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only the plateau regions listed as parts of the Central Highlands in the source?

options.A: Malwa, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand and Chota Nagpur
options.C: Chota Nagpur, Deccan, Anaimalai and Cardamom

questions.explanation: The source identifies Malwa, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand and Chota Nagpur as the plateaus included in the Central Highlands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Deccan Plateau lies mainly on which side of the Narmada River?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau lies south of the Narmada River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two mountain systems broadly bound the Deccan Plateau?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau is broadly bounded by the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological materials are specifically associated with the Deccan Plateau in the source?

options.A: Recent alluvial deposits and coral limestone
options.B: Ancient crystalline rocks and extensive basaltic lava formations in the northwest

questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau is composed of ancient crystalline rocks and extensive basaltic lava formations in the northwest.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which direction do the major rivers of the Deccan Plateau generally flow?
questions.explanation: The source states that the major rivers of the Deccan Plateau generally flow eastward.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Meghalaya Plateau is described in the source as an extension of which major physiographic unit?
questions.explanation: The Meghalaya Plateau is an extension of the Peninsular Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What separates the Meghalaya Plateau from the main block of the Peninsular Plateau?
questions.explanation: The Meghalaya Plateau is separated from the main block of the Peninsular Plateau by the Ganga–Brahmaputra alluvial lowlands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of hills belongs to the Meghalaya Plateau?
questions.explanation: The Meghalaya Plateau includes the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What type of rainfall is specifically associated with the Meghalaya Plateau in the source?
questions.explanation: The source notes that the Meghalaya Plateau receives very heavy orographic rainfall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among the major ranges and hills of the Peninsular Plateau?
questions.explanation: The source lists the Aravalli, Vindhya, Satpura, Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, Nilgiri, Anaimalai and Cardamom Hills as important ranges and hills of the Peninsular Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats?

options.A: The Eastern Ghats are generally higher and more continuous
options.B: The Western Ghats are generally higher and more continuous
options.C: Both are equally continuous throughout their length
options.D: The Western Ghats are located along the eastern plateau

questions.explanation: The source states that the Western Ghats are generally higher and more continuous than the discontinuous Eastern Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Aravalli Range is described in the source as one of the world's:
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range is identified as one of the world's ancient fold mountain systems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which broad direction does the Aravalli Range extend across Rajasthan towards Delhi?
questions.explanation: The source describes the Aravalli Range as extending broadly southwest–northeast across Rajasthan towards Delhi.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Vindhya Range is broadly located in which geographical position according to the source?
questions.explanation: The source places the Vindhya Range in the Central Indian highlands, broadly north of the Narmada Valley.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Between which two river valleys is the Satpura Range located?
questions.explanation: The Satpura Range lies between the Narmada and Tapi valleys.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which peak is identified as the highest point of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Dhupgarh, located in the Satpura Range, is identified in the source as the highest point of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which feature best describes the Western Ghats in the source?

options.A: A discontinuous chain along the eastern plateau
options.B: A continuous escarpment along the western edge of the Deccan
options.C: A low alluvial plain along the Bay of Bengal
options.D: A group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats form a continuous escarpment along the western edge of the Deccan Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two features are specifically associated with the Western Ghats in the source?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are associated with high biodiversity and orographic rainfall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which characteristic distinguishes the Eastern Ghats in the source?

options.A: They form a continuous wall along the western coast
options.B: They are discontinuous hills along the eastern plateau and are cut by major rivers
options.C: They are a chain of young fold mountains in the north
options.D: They consist entirely of coral limestone

questions.explanation: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous hills along the eastern plateau and are cut by major rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Nilgiri Hills are described as the meeting region of which two mountain systems?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Hills form the meeting region of the Western and Eastern Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills according to the source?
questions.explanation: Doddabetta is identified as the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Anaimalai Hills are located in which part of the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the Anaimalai Hills as part of the southern Western Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which important peak is located in the Anaimalai Hills according to the source?
questions.explanation: Anamudi lies in the Anaimalai Hills in Kerala and is identified as the highest peak in South India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Cardamom Hills are located in which broad region according to the source?

options.A: Southern Western Ghats in the Kerala–Tamil Nadu region
options.B: Northern Himalayas in the Ladakh region

questions.explanation: The Cardamom Hills are part of the southern Western Ghats in the Kerala–Tamil Nadu region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Deccan Trap is primarily composed of which type of rock?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Trap is a vast province of flood basalts formed by repeated volcanic eruptions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: During which geological period did the repeated volcanic eruptions that formed the Deccan Trap occur, according to the source?

options.A: Near the beginning of the Cambrian period
options.B: Near the end of the Cretaceous period

questions.explanation: The source states that the Deccan Trap formed through repeated volcanic eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous period.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the Deccan Trap given the name 'trap'?

options.B: Because it is covered by permanent ice
options.C: Because it forms a circular coastal lagoon
options.D: Because it consists of loose desert sand

questions.explanation: The step-like topography of the Deccan Trap gave it the name 'trap'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Weathering of which rock type in the Deccan Trap has produced extensive black regur soils?
questions.explanation: Weathering of basalt in the Deccan Trap has produced extensive black regur soils.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Mineral Resources of the Peninsular Plateau
questions.question: Which geological formations are identified as hosts for mineral deposits in the Peninsular Plateau?

options.A: Dharwar-type greenstone belts, sedimentary basins and igneous formations

questions.explanation: The source identifies ancient crystalline rocks, Dharwar-type greenstone belts, sedimentary basins and igneous formations as hosts for minerals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Mineral Resources of the Peninsular Plateau
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only minerals listed in the source as occurring in the Peninsular Plateau?

options.A: Iron ore, manganese, bauxite and mica
options.B: Petroleum, natural gas, salt and gypsum only
options.C: Coal, petroleum, coral and phosphate only
options.D: Diamond, salt, limestone and marine gas only

questions.explanation: The source lists iron ore, manganese, bauxite, mica, copper, gold and coal among the minerals hosted by the geological formations of the Peninsular Plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which Indian state is the Thar Desert mainly located?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert lies mainly in western Rajasthan and extends into Pakistan's Sindh and Punjab regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical region bounds the Thar Desert to the east according to the source?
questions.explanation: The source states that the Thar Desert is bounded by the Aravalli region to the east and merges with the Rann of Kachchh towards the south.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which rainfall pattern is characteristic of the Thar Desert according to the source?

options.A: Rainfall is high and evenly distributed throughout the year
options.B: Rainfall is very low and highly variable
options.D: Rainfall is uniform from east to west

questions.explanation: The Thar Desert receives very low and highly variable rainfall. Most rainfall arrives with the southwest monsoon, but totals decline westward.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common landform of the Thar Desert listed in the source?
questions.explanation: The source lists barchan and longitudinal dunes, sand sheets, interdunal depressions, playas, salt flats, pediments and rocky outcrops as common desert landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the source, which factors influence the shape and movement of desert dunes?

questions.question: What is one of the main purposes of developing satellite cities near large metropolitan centres?

options.B: To increase congestion in the core city
options.C: To prevent all movement between urban centres
options.D: To accommodate population and economic activity and reduce pressure on the core city

questions.explanation: Satellite cities are intended to accommodate population and economic activity while reducing pressure on the main metropolitan centre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified in the source as an example of a satellite city associated with Delhi?
questions.explanation: Gurugram is listed among the examples of satellite cities associated with the Delhi metropolitan area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group consists entirely of examples of satellite cities associated with Delhi mentioned in the source?
questions.explanation: The source lists Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad as examples of satellite cities associated with Delhi.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a satellite city associated with Delhi in the source?
questions.explanation: The examples given are Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad. Jaipur is not included in that list.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Satellite cities are generally located in relation to which type of settlement?
questions.explanation: Satellite cities are planned or functionally linked urban settlements located near a large metropolitan centre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a major housing-related problem in urban areas?

options.D: Decline in all forms of urban activity

questions.explanation: Housing shortages are identified as one of the major problems affecting urban areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common transport-related problem in urban areas?
questions.explanation: Traffic congestion is among the urban problems identified in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair consists of environmental problems commonly faced by urban areas?

options.C: Deforestation of all rural settlements and desert expansion only
options.D: Declining urban population and excessive agricultural land

questions.explanation: Air pollution and water scarcity are among the environmental challenges identified in the source's discussion of urban problems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only urban environmental and infrastructure problems identified in the source?

options.A: Glacier retreat, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
options.B: Soil formation, mineral extraction and crop rotation
options.C: Rural isolation, shifting cultivation and terrace farming
options.D: Sewage, solid waste, urban flooding and loss of wetlands

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The urban heat island effect is identified in the source as:
questions.explanation: Urban heat islands are included among the environmental problems associated with urban areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a social or service-access challenge in urban areas?

options.A: Uniform access to all urban services

questions.explanation: Unequal access to services is listed among the problems affecting urban areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination best represents the integrated approach to smart urban planning described in the source?

options.A: Land use, public transport, affordable housing, efficient resource use, green infrastructure and disaster resilience
options.B: Road construction alone, without housing or environmental planning
options.C: Exclusive focus on digital services without physical infrastructure
options.D: Industrial expansion without public spaces or basic services

questions.explanation: Smart urban planning integrates land use, public transport, affordable housing, water and energy efficiency, green infrastructure, digital services, disaster resilience and inclusive public spaces.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the source, what is the appropriate role of technology in smart urban planning?

options.A: Technology should replace all physical and social planning
options.B: Technology should be used only for traffic monitoring
options.C: Technology makes affordable housing and public transport unnecessary
options.D: Technology is a tool and cannot substitute for sound urban planning

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which broad geographical regions of India are predominantly associated with rice cultivation?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the eastern and coastal belts as broad rice-dominant agricultural regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which region of India is identified as predominantly wheat-dominant?
questions.explanation: The northwestern plains are identified as the major wheat-dominant agricultural region in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is associated with millet and pulse-producing drylands?

options.A: Punjab, Haryana, Bihar and West Bengal
options.C: Kerala, Goa, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: The source identifies the drylands of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka as millet- and pulse-dominant regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The major plantation agricultural belts of India are associated with which geographical regions?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the Western Ghats and Northeast as important plantation agricultural belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which states are identified as important irrigated sugarcane-producing regions?

options.D: Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: The source identifies irrigated sugarcane regions in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following agricultural region–crop combinations is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The eastern and coastal belts are identified as rice-dominant regions. The other combinations do not match the regional agricultural pattern described in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following pairs: 1. Northwestern plains – Wheat 2. Western Ghats and Northeast – Plantation crops 3. Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka – Millets and pulses. Which pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All three pairs correctly represent the broad agricultural regions identified in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which agricultural region is associated with both Maharashtra and Karnataka in the source?

options.B: Millet and pulse drylands as well as irrigated sugarcane regions
options.C: Only the eastern rice-dominant coastal belt

questions.explanation: Maharashtra and Karnataka are included among the millet and pulse dryland states. Both are also identified as irrigated sugarcane-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is associated with both millet and pulse drylands and irrigated sugarcane regions in the source?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is included in the millet and pulse dryland region and in the irrigated sugarcane region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement best represents the broad agricultural regional pattern described for India?

options.A: All major crops are concentrated in the northwestern plains
options.B: Plantation agriculture is restricted to Rajasthan and Gujarat
options.C: Rice and wheat are produced exclusively in the same agricultural belt
options.D: Different crops are associated with distinct broad regions, including rice belts, wheat plains, drylands, plantation belts and irrigated sugarcane areas

questions.explanation: The source describes a diverse agricultural geography in which different crops are associated with different broad geographical regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which states form the core of India's eastern and central mineral belt?

options.A: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and parts of Madhya Pradesh
options.B: Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh
options.C: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Karnataka

questions.explanation: The eastern and central mineral belt includes Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and parts of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two mineral resources are specifically identified as supporting steel and power industries in the eastern and central mineral belt?

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT included in the eastern and central mineral belt described in the source?
questions.explanation: The mineral belt identified in the source includes Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and parts of Madhya Pradesh. Punjab is not included in this list.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which set contains the petroleum and natural gas regions identified in the source?

options.A: Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, Sikkim and Goa
options.B: Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai Offshore, Rajasthan and the Krishna–Godavari basin
options.C: Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Tripura and Delhi
options.D: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Punjab

questions.explanation: The source identifies Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai Offshore, Rajasthan and the Krishna–Godavari basin as petroleum and natural gas regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which offshore region is specifically mentioned among India's petroleum and natural gas areas?
questions.explanation: Mumbai Offshore is specifically identified as one of the petroleum and natural gas regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Krishna–Godavari basin is identified in the source as an important region for which resources?
questions.explanation: The Krishna–Godavari basin is listed among the petroleum and natural gas regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which broad parts of India are identified as having strong solar and wind resources?
questions.explanation: The source identifies western and southern India as regions with strong solar and wind resources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following resource–region combinations is correctly matched?

options.A: Coal and iron ore – eastern and central mineral belt
options.B: Petroleum and gas – only the Himalayan region
options.C: Solar and wind – only the northeastern region
options.D: Petroleum and gas – exclusively the Thar Desert

questions.explanation: The eastern and central mineral belt contains coal and iron ore that support steel and power industries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Jharkhand and Odisha form part of the eastern and central mineral belt. 2. Assam and Gujarat are among the petroleum and gas regions. 3. Western and southern India have strong solar and wind resources. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are supported by the regional mineral and energy distribution described in the source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement best explains the relationship between the eastern and central mineral belt and industrial development?

options.A: The belt supports only plantation agriculture
options.B: Coal and iron ore resources support steel and power industries
options.C: The belt is important only for international tourism
options.D: Its mineral resources are unrelated to industrial activity

questions.explanation: The source explicitly links coal and iron ore from the eastern and central mineral belt with steel and power industries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are regional inequalities?

options.A: Differences in climate between two seasons
options.B: Differences in the length of rivers between states
options.D: Differences in income, infrastructure, employment, education, health, connectivity and access to resources

questions.explanation: Regional inequalities refer to differences in several dimensions of development, including income, infrastructure, employment, education, health, connectivity and resource access.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Regional inequalities may occur:

options.B: Only between rural and urban settlements
options.C: Both between states and within individual states
options.D: Only between coastal and island regions

questions.explanation: The source explains that regional inequalities exist both between states and within states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a factor contributing to regional inequalities?
questions.explanation: Historical investment is one of the factors that contribute to regional inequalities, along with geography, governance, industrial structure, urbanisation and human capital.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only factors identified as contributing to regional inequalities?

options.A: Latitude, longitude, tides and ocean currents
options.B: Historical investment, geography, governance and industrial structure
options.C: Monsoon duration, lunar phases, eclipses and earthquakes
options.D: River length, mountain height, soil colour and day length

questions.explanation: Historical investment, geography, governance and industrial structure are among the factors identified in the source. Urbanisation and human-capital differences also contribute.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Differences in which of the following are included in the concept of regional inequalities?
questions.explanation: Regional inequalities include differences in education, health, employment and connectivity, in addition to income, infrastructure and access to resources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about regional inequalities is correct?

options.A: They are caused exclusively by physical geography
options.B: They are limited to differences in agricultural production
options.C: They reflect the combined influence of historical, geographical, governance, industrial, urbanisation and human-capital factors
options.D: They occur only between different countries

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical factor can influence the cost and movement of goods in trade?

options.A: Location relative to markets and ports
options.B: The number of historical monuments alone
options.C: The administrative language of a region alone
options.D: The population of a region's capital alone

questions.explanation: Location relative to markets and ports is one of the geographical factors affecting trade and the movement and cost of goods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a transport-related factor affecting trade?
questions.explanation: Transport networks influence the movement and cost of goods and are an important geographical factor affecting trade.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only factors that affect trade according to the source?

options.A: Rainfall, soil colour, vegetation type and altitude only
options.B: Markets, ports, transport networks, resources, labour and energy
options.C: Population age, literacy and birth rate only
options.D: Religious festivals, languages and historical monuments only

questions.explanation: The source identifies markets, ports, transport networks, natural resources, labour and energy among the factors affecting trade. Climate, topography, border access, logistics and trade agreements also matter.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why do coastal regions often have an advantage in trade?

options.A: They are always closer to every inland market
options.B: They do not require transport infrastructure
options.C: They are unaffected by global demand
options.D: They often benefit from access to ports

questions.explanation: Coastal regions often benefit from port access, which can facilitate the movement of goods to and from overseas markets.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Landlocked regions generally depend on which facilities for access to external trade routes?
questions.explanation: The source explains that landlocked regions depend on inland corridors because they do not have direct coastal port access.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts the trade-related geographical advantages of coastal and landlocked regions?

options.A: Both always have direct access to seaports
options.B: Landlocked regions generally have better port access than coastal regions
options.C: Coastal regions often benefit from port access, while landlocked regions depend on inland corridors
options.D: Neither coastal nor landlocked regions require transport networks

questions.explanation: The source specifically contrasts coastal regions, which often benefit from port access, with landlocked regions, which depend on inland corridors.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which factor is relevant to trade because it influences the movement and cost of goods across international boundaries?

options.C: The number of inland lakes alone
options.D: The age of nearby mountain ranges

questions.explanation: Border access and trade agreements are among the factors affecting trade and the movement and cost of goods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are export-oriented industries?

options.A: Industries that produce exclusively for local village markets
options.B: Industries that manufacture only agricultural equipment
options.C: Industries that operate without transport or logistics
options.D: Industries that produce goods and services for overseas markets

questions.explanation: Export-oriented industries produce goods and services intended for overseas markets.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the principal purpose of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) as described in the source?

options.A: To provide designated infrastructure and regulatory arrangements that support export activity
options.B: To prohibit the production of goods for overseas markets
options.C: To replace all existing transport networks
options.D: To restrict industrial activity to agricultural regions

questions.explanation: SEZs provide designated infrastructure and regulatory arrangements intended to support export activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a factor determining the effectiveness of an SEZ?

options.A: Its distance from every transport network
options.D: The complete absence of supply chains

questions.explanation: Connectivity is one of the factors affecting SEZ effectiveness. Skills, policy stability, supply chains and global demand are also important.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination contains all the factors listed in the source as influencing the effectiveness of SEZs?

options.A: Climate, rainfall, soil fertility and river depth
options.B: Connectivity, skills, policy stability, supply chains and global demand
options.C: Population density, birth rate, literacy and sex ratio
options.D: Mineral reserves, forest cover, altitude and slope

questions.explanation: The source identifies connectivity, skills, policy stability, supply chains and global demand as factors determining the effectiveness of SEZs.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about export-oriented industries and SEZs: 1. Export-oriented industries produce goods and services for overseas markets. 2. SEZs provide designated infrastructure and regulatory arrangements. 3. SEZ effectiveness depends only on the availability of land. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are supported by the source. Statement 3 is incorrect because SEZ effectiveness depends on several factors, including connectivity, skills, policy stability, supply chains and global demand.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement best explains the relationship between geographical conditions and the movement of goods in trade?

options.A: Trade is influenced only by the number of factories
options.B: Geographical factors have no influence on transport costs
options.C: Markets, ports, transport, resources, topography, labour, energy and logistics can influence trade routes and costs
options.D: Only climate determines the direction of international trade

questions.explanation: The source presents trade as being influenced by several geographical and economic factors, including location, markets, ports, transport, resources, climate, topography, labour, energy and logistics.

questions.question: Which of the following statements provides the most comprehensive explanation of India's economic and regional geography?

options.A: Economic geography is determined exclusively by the distribution of minerals

options.C: Regional development depends only on the physical size of states
options.D: Trade, industry and agriculture operate independently of geographical conditions

questions.explanation: The section brings together agricultural regions, mineral and energy regions, regional inequalities, geographical factors affecting trade, and export-oriented industries and SEZs as major components of economic and regional geography.
